purpose: Audit and exercise the captured organ surface meshes as render-only surfaces directly bound to FEM rest nodes.

method.simulation_geometry: Unchanged tetrahedral FEM assets in tet/*.npz
method.binding: Nearest rest-node correspondence with unique-node and 10 micrometre maximum-error guards; live render vertices index the same FEM particle positions
method.mesh_rejection: Non-watertight, inconsistent-winding, ambiguous, or out-of-tolerance meshes fall back to the FEM boundary surface

runtime_comparison.visual_review: The outputs are nearly indistinguishable at this camera scale. This confirms successful runtime use of the bound surfaces but does not show a meaningful visual-detail gain; the source meshes are not high-resolution assets.

deformation_runtime.scope: Confirms the source render vertices follow live FEM nodes during a short scripted episode. This run did not evaluate element inversion, calibrated contact, task success, or realism.

limitations: Captured PLY surfaces have slightly fewer triangles than the corresponding FEM boundaries and do not add higher-resolution geometry.
About 1.7-3.5% of captured triangles are not identical to FEM boundary facets, even though the captured meshes are closed and their vertices bind uniquely to FEM nodes.
No sub-surface rendering, calibrated albedo, camera-to-surface video registration, or expert visual validation is established.
The broad endoscope composition and faceted surrounding anatomy still fail the visual realism gate.
privacy: No source video, rendered image, absolute user path, or personal metadata is included in this report; runtime images remain in ignored local output folders.
